XPENC can't read or answer the *99# menu for you — that screen belongs to your phone's own dialer, not any app. What this does instead:

2. Tap Dial *99# — XPENC copies it and opens your dialer, ready to call.
3. You go through the menu yourself: Send Money → paste → amount → UPI PIN.
4. Back in XPENC, log it as a normal transaction.

Trends over time, spending-by-category charts, and Standings — a ranked top-transactions/top-categories list for the period.
Switch periods from the top of the screen; tap any category slice or Standings row to jump into its own detail.

A money-first view across every account: total money, money in and out this month or year, and seven reports — Balances, Activity per account, Balance history, Transfers between accounts, Payment methods, Cards & pay later, and Account health (accounts below zero, under their minimum, or sitting idle).
Switch Month/Year and step through periods at the top, then tap a report tile. Tap any account row to open its own statement.
Exports your whole ledger to CSV or JSON — for a spreadsheet, a backup you keep yourself, or moving your data elsewhere.
Pick a format and share/save the resulting file.

Manual backups plus scheduled auto-backups, with a choice of retention rule (keep the last N, or a time window). Restoring replaces the current ledger with a backup's contents — the safety net for switching phones or undoing a mistake.
Back up any time from this screen; auto-backups run on their own schedule once turned on. Long-press to batch-select several backups to delete at once.

Money in and out categories, each with its own icon and colour, picked from a searchable icon sheet. Tap one to see how much went to it — this month, this year or all time — split by subcategory, with every transaction behind the figure.

Save your whole category structure as a named template and switch between saved templates any time — switching never touches a transaction. The archive button lists archived categories to restore, or to delete one nothing has ever used.
Labels that cut across categories — a tag isn't tied to money in or out, so it can mark anything that shares a context (e.g. "Trip to Goa").
Tag groups bundle tags that always go together (e.g. "Work trip" = Travel + Meals) so you pick the whole set at once from the tag picker.

Currency (including ones you create), theme, your own colours for money in, out, transfers and people, the day the week starts, security (PIN, master password, and/or an authenticator app — any combination you turn on unlocks the app), notifications, permissions such as contacts, the app level (Basic/Medium/Pro), budget cycle start day, and which tabs show in the bottom nav.
Everything here takes effect immediately, no save button.
Travel spends, split with friends, abroad or at home
A wedding, a festival, a move — set it up your way
For an annual subscription or insurance — it repeats on the day and month it starts.
With a rate saved in Settings → Currencies, typing what it cost there fills in the amount here.
Move money between goals, or pay a loan from one. Hide Transfer in / out on any account from Edit account.
On each due date, what’s left of the statement moves from the account you pick — nothing if it’s already paid.
Your card's statement, as it closed
See what the statement said, what you’ve paid since and what’s left by the due date. New purchases build the next statement.
Any day up to the 31st, or the last working day of the month — Dashboard, Budgets and Stats run payday to payday.
Send your category structure as a file, import one someone shared, or start from the ready-made 50/30/20 — Needs and Wants. More templates, from the community too, are on xpenc.in/templates.
Pick 50%, 80%, 100% — any levels you like. Each one alerts once a period, so you feel the spending climb.
What you own, what you owe
Total money now shows its two halves: everything in credit, and every card bill and loan you still owe.
Drag your accounts into the order you want. The Dashboard and Accounts both follow it, and new accounts join the end.
Away for a month, or paid it another way? Skip the next date only — nothing posts, and the rule carries on from the one after.
Slide between Image and PDF, pick the period, then send it straight into their WhatsApp or Messages chat. When they owe you, a QR of your UPI ID with the amount lets them scan and pay.

Your money on hand 3, 6 or 12 months from now: auto rules on the dates they post, plus your usual spending from the last 3 months. See the lowest point too — and the day you’d run short, if you would.
Buttons and tabs answer your touch instantly, sheets stretch and spring back, the month picker frosts over, and lists fade softly under the top bar. On a tablet the tab bar sits centred.
Money in, money out or a reminder, already dated to the day you picked. Wandered off to another day? Today takes you straight back.

Add a person straight from your Connector friends, or hold someone already here to link them. They show as @username. On a phone it reads the list the Connector app shares — XPENC still never goes online.
Backups from Connector come in by themselves

Connector pulled a newer backup from your other phone? XPENC takes it in as it opens — on its own when nothing here would be lost, after asking when this phone has changes of its own. A copy is saved first. XPENC still never touches the internet.
Backups no longer hold your PIN, recovery phrase or authenticator secret, and importing another phone’s backup keeps this phone’s own PIN length — so your PIN always still types.

A preview of XPENC in your browser — offline, your data stays in that browser. Bring a phone backup over with Import from file, or turn on Connector there (Settings → Connector) to keep it in sync with your phones.
A mode is now its own little app

Switch a trip ON and the app is the trip: the home shows what’s left to spend and how much a day, Persons shows only the people with you (starting from zero), each account shows what you gave the trip, and limits ask before you go over. Split bills with your people, plan costs up front, fill a trip wallet — and share the summary at the end.

Set up a trip — dates, budget, the accounts and categories it uses, tags for every spend — and switch it ON. Everything you add joins it, and the app shows only what the trip needs. Afterwards it’s one line in Transactions that opens into the whole story.
How much went to it this month, this year or all time — split by subcategory for a parent — with every transaction behind the figure.
Pay straight from a savings goal
Turn it on and the goal works like a pocket of your bank account: pick it for money in or money out, and its balance moves with them. Off by default — a goal stays transfer-only until you say so.
Transfer in / out from an account

One tap starts a transfer with that account already filled in. Keep cash at home as its own account and withdraw from it into your wallet like an ATM — Add account → Cash suggests Cash at home (V-ATM).
Every entry shows the balance right after it, like a bank passbook — the same figure your statement PDF prints. Off by default.
Move money on a schedule between your own accounts — bank to cash, a card bill, into a goal or towards a loan. It replaces G&L; goal and loan rules work as before.
Tags on money lent and borrowed
Tag an entry like any transaction — each one shows its tags on the person’s page, and when the money moved through an account, its transaction carries them too, so it turns up when you filter by tag.
For a currency XPENC doesn’t list: a three-letter code, a symbol, a name and its decimal places. It works like any other — as your parent currency, an account’s own, or with an exchange rate.
Start the week on Sunday or Monday
The Calendar tab and every date picker follow it. Monday is the default.
Contacts stay closed when access is off
Say no to contacts access, or turn it off, and every “from contacts” button goes away — XPENC never opens your address book without it. Turn it back on here and they return.
Income and Expense are now Money in and Money out — a refund or a meal voucher isn’t income, and not every payment is an expense. Your data and backups don’t change.
Choose the colour for money in, money out, transfers and people — from the swatches or any hex colour. Transaction icons can follow their category, the money colour, or one colour for all.
All your accounts in one card
Pick One card to see every account and its balance at a glance, with nothing to swipe. Slider keeps the row of cards.
Change an account’s icon and colour
Rename it and pick a new colour and icon together — two accounts that looked alike no longer have to be deleted and re-created.
Restore any archived category — a parent brings its subcategories back. One that was never used can be deleted for good.
Pick a profile photo from your gallery — no contact needed. It’s shrunk to avatar size and kept on your phone.
Your own emoji as a category icon
Tap ➕ under Emoji and type any emoji with your keyboard — 🍕 for food, 🐶 for the dog. It shows wherever that category does, and the emoji you’ve used stay one tap away for the next one.
The same app, now on iPhone through SideStore or AltStore. A backup made here restores there and the other way round, so switching phones doesn’t mean starting over.
Share as a PDF or an image

Pick PDF for a clean, printable document — a receipt for a transaction, a statement with a running balance for a person, every expense and who owes whom for a group. Pick Image for a styled card, dark or light, ready for any chat.

Turn it on and the transaction shows as a frosted “Hidden · hold to view” row everywhere it’s listed, so a screenshot or screen recording only catches the frost. Hold the row to see it — screenshots and recordings are blocked while you do, and while its own page is open.
Drag widgets into the order you want, take off the ones you don’t, and add new ones: Cash flow, Savings goals, Loans, Shortcuts, Groups and Shopping lists.
Pick a past month and the Dashboard shows it as it closed: its opening and closing balance, account balances and who owed whom on its last day, and its own transactions.

Every module now has a row of shortcuts to the pages that go with it — Currency from Accounts, Categories from Budgets, Tags and Payees from Transactions, and more. On the Dashboard, tap Total money to pick which accounts count toward it.
Glass grows out of what you tap

Switch tabs and the top bar resizes to the new tab’s buttons. Settled, Archived and Inbox grow down out of the top bar; New group grows out of its button; pages from More open on a calmer spring. The Transactions filters sit on frosted glass, and a person’s photo lights their card with its own colour.

The tab bar now transforms into whatever you open from it: every sheet and every page in More grows up out of the bar on a spring and folds back into it when you close it. A quick action makes the ➕ itself swell into the page. Search on Transactions turns the top bar into the search field. And the glass takes the light of what's behind it — scroll something colourful under the tab bar and its edge glows with that colour.
Glass quick actions, and smoother everything

Hold the ➕ and your quick actions spring out onto two arcs in the corner — slide your thumb to one and let go, and the ➕ swells into its page. XPENC also runs at your screen’s full refresh rate now (90/120 Hz where the phone supports it), with calmer, smoother motion throughout Glass. The top bar is now a floating glass capsule too: tabs scroll under it to the top of the screen, the big title flies into it as you scroll, and the tab bar grows into the month picker. Person photos now show on their transactions too, Persons scrolls under the bar and its switch, and hidden amounts turn to frosted glass.
New themes: Classic, Noir and Glass

Glass is Liquid Glass, like iPhone: frosted cards, a floating tab bar with a sliding glass droplet, large titles under glass buttons, floating sheets, iOS icons and switches, swipe-back pages and bouncy scrolling — on a background you pick: Aurora, White, Black, Ocean, Sunset or Nebula. Noir (was Bold) is heavier and bolder and now has a light version too. Light, Dark or System is now its own choice. Colourful, Midnight and Cove are retired; if you used one, you are on Classic, with your light or dark choice kept.

Pick one of your people as the payee — like money given to a parent that is not coming back. It shows on their page in a small "As payee" list but never counts toward owe/due. Add people or payees straight from contacts; someone already saved is reused, never duplicated. In Payees, "Connect to person" joins a payee to someone in People.

Hold the ➕ and a ring of 8 shortcuts opens mid-screen — slide toward one to open it, or back to ✕ in the centre to cancel. Any slot can be a screen, a calculator, Add money in/out or a saved transaction template. Your old 3 shortcuts carry over.

When someone's balance reaches zero, XPENC now asks: Move to Settled, Archive, or Keep here — nothing disappears on its own. Settled people and groups keep their history and move back by themselves the moment money is owed again.
Delete now works even with history: every entry and group expense goes with it, and the money they moved is put back in your accounts. The confirm dialog says exactly how much will be removed.

FD & RD, Loan EMI with a year-wise schedule and prepayment savings, SIP & Lumpsum with yearly step-up, PPF, GST, and Income Tax for India (new vs old regime), the US, the UK and Germany. Results update as you type.

App says ₹100 in cash but your wallet has ₹75? Enter what you really have and the difference is saved as one "Correction" — no made-up payment, and your history stays as it was. Corrections never count as money in or out, but they lower the XPENC Score's Tracking habit, so logging as you go still pays off.

Money in and out for any month or year, plus seven reports: Balances, Activity per account, Balance history for any account, Transfers between accounts, Payment methods, Cards & pay later (spent, repaid, next due) and Account health — accounts below zero, under their minimum or sitting unused.
Add loans that started years ago

Dates now go back to 2000, and the first auto-payment can start on the loan's own start date — every past EMI is posted the moment you save, split into interest and principal. Older dates show their year, so a 2017 payment never looks like this year's.

An EMI's interest always gets a category (the loan's, the rule's, or EMI), you can name the lender as payee on a loan's Auto rule, and the payment card now says Interest and Principal. The loan screen no longer shows a "You're saving" amount when you haven't paid extra.
Who owes whom in a group
Each member's net balance, the fewest payments that settle the group, and every pairwise debt with the expenses behind it. Group expenses also carry a tappable group tag.
Nothing hidden under the nav bar
The last item of every list now scrolls clear of Android's gesture bar or buttons, so you can always reach and tap it.
Contacts access is off. Turn it on in Settings → Permissions.
Share of money in left after money out over the last 90 days. 30% or more earns full points; 0% or less earns none.
Of the last 3 full months, how many ended with money out at or below money in.
Monthly debt obligations as a share of monthly money in — loan EMIs, credit card and pay-later dues, plus a third of what you owe people. 20% or less earns full points; 60% or more earns none.
A payment into every active loan in each of the last 3 full months, and no overdue amounts owed to people.
Cash, bank, prepaid and savings-goal balances measured in months of average spending. 6 months or more earns full points.
Share of your budgets still within their limit this period.

Days with at least one entry in the last 30. 12 or more earns full points — the score is only as accurate as the ledger behind it. Each balance correction in the same 30 days takes away a quarter, since it means entries were missed.
Its balance can be moved into the goal next.
Heavy type, ink outlines, coral & gold
English, Hindi, German, Japanese and Russian are built in, and it follows your phone. Import a language pack for more.
Refunds give back to a budget
Money back from a purchase goes to its spending category, so the budget shows what you really kept.
Total money counts every account. Accounts you switch off leave only Available balance.
Any folder inside Download, like Download/backup/xpenc.
